Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Objections to the Specification:
In paragraph [0058], of line 8 contains improper grammar and is improperly omitting a coma within the phrase “and thus the computer readable medium” and in order to restore proper grammar will be interpreted as “and thus, the computer readable medium” for the purposes of this opinion.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 102:
The following is a quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for the rejections under this section made in this Office action: A person shall be entitled to a patent unless –
(a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
(a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
Claims 1-4, 7-11, 14-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C 102(a1) as being anticipated by US 10262240 B2 to GUO, Y et al. (hereinafter “GUO”).
As per claim 1, GUO discloses a method, comprising: generating, by a system comprising a processor (a method carried out by a system comprising a processor for computing in order to generate extraction features based on the instructions executed by the processor; figure 2; abstract; column 2, lines 10-60), a feature extraction layer portion of an image classification model based on a deep neural network “DNN” model (a feature extraction process (layer) of a classifier 110 (classification model) using a deep neural network DNN model in order to train the classifier 110 on training data set 102; figure 2; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-25); extracting a group of features of a group of images by using the feature extraction layer portion (extracting data via the classifier 110 using input image 112 and extracting features of said image 112 in order to identify various classes 114 associated with the image 112; figure 2; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-25); training an output layer portion of the image classification model according to features of the group of features of training images in the group of images and according to classification labels of the training images (training via the training data set 102 such that classifier 214 can produce outputs (output layer) via the DNN wherein the output is determined via derived value features which were trained into the model during learning steps which allow the classifier model to learn various classes and other classification labels relevant to the images; figure 2; column 3, lines 13-62; column 4, lines 4-59); and generating the image classification model by combining the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion (wherein the feature extraction process and the output process are both conducted via the classifier 110 and are therefore combined into the classifier 110 to provide the overall image classification model; figure 2-3; column 3, lines 13-62; column 4, lines 4-59).
As per claim 2, GUO discloses the method according to claim 1, wherein the DNN model has more categories than the image classification model (a categorical distribution is utilized within the system wherein the SoftMax function determines the categorical distribution in multi class classification methods; figures 2-3; column 5, lines 4-24).
As per claim 3, GUO discloses the method according to claim 1, further comprising: storing the group of features of the group of images, resulting in a stored group of features (wherein the features selected are stored in a computer-based memory which has storage functionality to store computer executable instructions; figures 2-3; column 11, lines 19-30).
As per claim 4, GUO discloses the method according to claim 3, further comprising: acquiring the features of the training images by accessing at least some of the stored group of features (the features provided as stored instructions in mass storage device 916 adapted to act as a machine readable medium 922 storage device and has the ability to access a plurality of feature classification layers and determine the weight provided to said feature; figures 2-3; column 11, lines 19-51; CLAIM 12-13).
As per claim 7, GUO discloses a system, comprising: at least one processing unit (the system comprises a computer processor; figures 2-3; column 11, lines 19-51); and at least one memory that is coupled to the at least one processing unit and stores instructions for execution by the at least one processing unit (a static memory 906 that includes a hardware processor 902 which executes instructions 924 via the processor 902 wherein said instructions 924 are stored on memory 906; figures 2-3; column 11, lines 19-51), the at least one processing unit comprising: a feature extraction unit (the system which includes a processor further includes a feature extraction system; figure 2; column 4, lines 4-37; column 11, lines 19-51), comprising at least a portion of a deep neural network “DNN” model and configured to extract a group of features of a group of images (a feature extraction process (layer) of a classifier 110 (classification model) using a deep neural network DNN model in order to train the classifier 110 on training data set 102; figure 2; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-25); and an image classification model generation unit (wherein the extracted features resulting in the production of generating an image classifier 110 (model) adapted to classify images by associated features; figure 2; column 3, lines 40-46; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-25), configured to: train an output layer portion of an image classification model according to features of the group of features of training images in the group of images and according to labels of the training images (training via the training data set 102 such that classifier 214 can produce outputs (output layer) via the DNN wherein the output is determined via derived value features which were trained into the model during learning steps which allow the classifier model to learn various classes and other classification labels relevant to the images; column 3, lines 13-62; column 4, lines 4-59); and generate the image classification model by combining the at least a portion of the DNN model and the output layer portion of the trained image classification model (wherein the feature extraction process and the output process are both conducted via the classifier 110 and are therefore combined into the classifier 110 to provide the overall image classification model; column 3, lines 13-62; column 4, lines 4-59), resulting in a generated image classification model (resulting in the production of generating an image classifier 110 (model) adapted to classify images by associated features; column 3, lines 40-46).
As per claim 8, GUO discloses the system according to claim 7, wherein the DNN model classifies according to more categories than the image classification model (a categorical distribution is utilized within the system wherein the SoftMax function determines the categorical distribution in multi class classification methods; figure 2; column 5, lines 4-24).
As per claim 9, GUO discloses the system according to claim 7, wherein the at least one processing unit further comprises: an image feature storage unit, configured to store the group of features of the group of images extracted by the feature extraction unit (wherein the features selected are stored in a computer-based memory which has storage functionality to store computer executable instructions; column 11, lines 19-30).
As per claim 10, GUO discloses the system according to claim 9, wherein the image classification model generation unit is further configured to obtain the features of the training images by accessing the image feature storage unit (the features provided as stored instructions in mass storage device 916 adapted to act as a machine readable medium 922 storage device and has the ability to access a plurality of feature classification layers and determine the weight provided to said feature; column 11, lines 19-51; CLAIM 12-13).
As per claim 11, GUO discloses the system according to claim 7, wherein the image classification model generation unit is further configured to further adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model based on the training images and the classification labels of the training images (the classifier model is trained via a predetermined distribution wherein the training parameters may be changed as desired wherein the parameters are learned from a predecessor network and uses an image classification probability function; column 3, lines 1-29).
As per claim 14, GUO discloses a non-transitory computer-readable medium, comprising machine-executable instructions that (a static memory 906 that includes a hardware processor 902 which executes instructions 924 via the processor 902 wherein said instructions 924 are stored on memory 906; figure 3; abstract; column 2, lines 10-60; column 11, lines 19-51), in response to execution by a device using a processor (the instructions 924 are executed via processor 902; figure 3; column 11, lines 19-51), cause the device to perform operations, comprising: generating a feature extraction layer portion of an image classification model based on a deep neural network “DNN” model (generating a feature extraction process (layer) of a classifier 110 (classification model) using a deep neural network DNN model in order to train the classifier 110 on training data set 102; figures 2-3; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-25); extracting a group of features of a group of images by using the feature extraction layer portion (wherein the extracted features resulting in the production of generating an image classifier 110 (model) adapted to classify images by associated features; figure 2; column 3, lines 30-62; column 4, lines 4-59); training an output layer portion of the image classification model according to features of the group of features of training images in the group of images and according to classification labels of the training images (training via the training data set 102 such that classifier 214 can produce outputs (output layer) via the DNN wherein the output is determined via derived value features which were trained into the model during learning steps which allow the classifier model to learn various classes and other classification labels relevant to the images; figures 2-3; column 3, lines 13-62; column 4, lines 4-59); and generating the image classification model by combining the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion (wherein the feature extraction process and the output process are both conducted via the classifier 110 and are therefore combined into the classifier 110 to provide the overall image classification model; figures 2-3; column 3, lines 40-62; column 4, lines 4-59).
As per claim 15, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 14, wherein the DNN model has more categories than the image classification model (a categorical distribution is utilized within the system wherein the SoftMax function determines the categorical distribution in multi class classification methods; column 5, lines 4-24).
As per claim 16, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 14, wherein the operations further comprise: storing the group of features of the group of images, resulting in a stored group of features (wherein the features selected are stored in a computer-based memory which has storage functionality to store computer executable instructions; column 11, lines 19-30).
As per claim 17, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 16, wherein the operations further comprise: acquiring the features of the training images by accessing at least some of the stored group of features (the features provided as stored instructions in mass storage device 916 adapted to act as a machine readable medium 922 storage device and has the ability to access a plurality of feature classification layers and determine the weight provided to said feature; column 11, lines 19-51; CLAIM 12-13).
As per claim 18, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 14, wherein the generating the image classification model results in a generated image classification model (resulting in the production of generating an image classifier 110 (model) adapted to classify images by associated features; column 3, lines 1-46), and wherein the operations further comprise: further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model based on the training images and the classification labels of the training images (the classifier model is trained via a predetermined distribution wherein the training parameters may be changed as desired wherein the parameters are learned from a predecessor network and uses an image classification probability function; column 3, lines 1-29).
Claim Rejections – 35 USC § 103:
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in this Office action: A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made. The factual inquiries for establishing a background for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 are summarized as follows:
1. Determining the scope and contents of the prior art.
2. Ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue.
3. Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art.
4. Considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or non-obviousness.
Claims 5-6, 12-13, and 19-20 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over GUO in view of US 10742399 B2 to CHEN, YEN-KUANG et al. (hereinafter “CHEN”).
As per claim 5, GUO discloses the method according to claim 1. GUO fails to disclose wherein the generating the image classification model results in a generated image classification model, and further comprising: further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model based on the training images and the classification labels of the training images.
CHEN discloses wherein the generating the image classification model results in a generated image classification model (wherein the system generates butterfly layers for image classification are adapted to separate clusters of data and combine the layers in order to classify said images; column 47, lines 3- 58), and further comprising: further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model based on the training images and the classification labels of the training images (wherein the system can be adjusted over any number of data points wherein in the example provided the desired data points are four data points which correspond to said clusters and process the points until all of the clusters are sorted into reference labels (classification label) to sort said data; column 46, lines 20-33; column 47, lines 3- 58; column 49, lines 8-23).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the method of GUO to provide wherein the generating the image classification model results in a generated image classification model, and further comprising: further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model based on the training images and the classification labels of the training images, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide the ability to use a plurality of data points up to the amount desired by the user (CHEN column 49, lines 8-23).
As per claim 6, GUO discloses the method according to claim 5. GUO fails to disclose wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels.
CHEN discloses wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels (the model is trained by using fully decompressed data points (original data) of the deep learning neural networks in order to visualize data directly and to properly label and classify said data via the model; column 46, lines 20-33; column 47, lines 3- 58; column 49, lines 8-23).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the method of GUO to provide wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide the ability to visualize data directly (column 46, lines 20-33).
As per claim 12, GUO discloses the system according to claim 11. GUO fails to disclose wherein the image classification model generation unit is further configured to train the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels.
CHEN discloses wherein the image classification model generation unit is further configured to train the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels (the model is trained by using fully decompressed data points (original data) of the deep learning neural networks in order to visualize data directly and to properly label and classify said data via the model; column 46, lines 20-33; column 47, lines 3- 58; column 49, lines 8-23).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the system of GUO to provide wherein the image classification model generation unit is further configured to train the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide the ability to visualize data directly (column 46, lines 20-33).
As per claim 13, GUO discloses the system according to claim 11. GUO fails to disclose wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit.
CHEN discloses wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit (the system utilizes a graphics processor in order to exchange image information which includes feature data and image output data within the system; column 19, lines 7-55; column 47, lines 3- 58).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the system of GUO to provide wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide a graphics processing unit to handle the computing resources required to analyze and sort the amount of image data available to the system (GUO column 19, lines 7-55).
As per claim 19, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 18. GUO fails to disclose wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels.
CHEN discloses wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels (the model is trained by using fully decompressed data points (original data) of the deep learning neural networks in order to visualize data directly and to properly label and classify said data via the model; column 46, lines 20-33; column 47, lines 3- 58; column 49, lines 8-23).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the system of GUO to provide wherein further adjusting the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the generated image classification model comprises: training the image classification model by using original data of the training images and the classification labels, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide the ability to visualize data directly (column 46, lines 20-33).
As per claim 20, GUO discloses the non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 19. GUO fails to disclose wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit.
CHEN discloses wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit (the system utilizes a graphics processor in order to exchange image information which includes feature data and image output data within the system; column 19, lines 7-55; column 47, lines 3- 58).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to modify the system of GUO to provide wherein the image classification model is further configured to adjust the feature extraction layer portion and the output layer portion of the image classification model by using at least one graphics processing unit, as taught by CHEN, in order to provide a graphics processing unit to handle the computing resources required to analyze and sort the amount of image data available to the system (GUO column 19, lines 7-55).
Conclusion:
